elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. It rises overall, with intervening declines, from 234.3 million in 2015 to a high of 375.7 million in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations
elements.description: The graphic breaks down 2025 external debt into public and publicly guaranteed debt and short-term debt, then subdivides public and publicly guaranteed debt by creditor type. Bilateral creditors account for 199.1 million, more than multilateral creditors at 149.9 million and private creditors at 10.0 million. Portugal is the largest named bilateral creditor at 90.3 million; other multilateral creditors account for 77.2 million.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show debt and debt-service ratios from 2015 to 2025 against a shaded range for DRS reporting countries. The 2025 external debt-to-exports ratio is the highest displayed ratio at 194%, while debt service-to-GNI is the lowest at 1%. External debt-to-exports rises to a mid-period peak and then falls; external debt-to-GNI generally declines.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: The left box, Official creditors, lists a maturity of 13 years, a grace period of 5 years and an interest rate of 0.2%, with a small horizontal indicator beneath each. The right box, Private creditors, shows '..' for maturity, grace period and interest rate, with empty indicator tracks. No private-creditor data values are shown because the country had no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
